Question: Which statement about flash points is correct?

Options:
A. It is the lowest concentration at which vapours of the substance will automatic start burning even without ignition source.
B. It is the lowest concentration at which vapours of the substance will have sustained fire if once ignited with ignition source
C. It is the lowest temperature at which vapours of the substance will automatic start burning even without presence of ignition source
D. It is the lowest temperature at which vapours of the substance will have sustained fire in the presence of ignition source
E. It is the lowest temperature at which vapours of the substance will have unsustained fire in presence of ignition source

Thought: I need to determine the correct definition of a flash point in chemistry. Let me analyze each option:

A. This describes an auto-ignition concentration, not a flash point.
B. This is about concentration, but flash point is a temperature property.
C. This describes auto-ignition temperature, not flash point.
D. This sounds closest to the definition of flash point - it's the lowest temperature at which vapors can be ignited by an external source and sustain combustion.
E. This is similar to D but mentions "unsustained" fire, which is not correct for flash point.

The flash point of a substance is the lowest temperature at which its vapors will ignite (but not necessarily continue to burn) when given an ignition source. Option D is the closest match, though it mentions "sustained fire" which is technically more characteristic of the fire point (which is slightly higher than the flash point).
Final Answer: The flash point is the lowest temperature at which vapors of a volatile material can ignite when given an ignition source. Option D is the most accurate description among the choices.
